embit.BIP375-I10: embit holds the key for this input, so it drops the per-input ECDH share that has no DLEQ proof and writes a correct global share instead. The PSBT it returns is valid. BIP 375 only requires verifying proofs for inputs the signer has no key for, so whether this counts as a failure is an open question for the maintainers.
embit.BIP375-I12: Same as I10 with an invalid DLEQ proof: embit replaces the bad per-input share with a correct global one and the returned PSBT is valid. Open question: refuse, or repair fields on inputs the signer controls?
embit.BIP375-I14: embit replaces the per-input share, but the input still has no BIP 32 derivation, so other parties cannot verify the returned PSBT.
embit.S3a: embit does not check that the supplied previous transaction hashes to the input's txid. The library has verify() for this, but sign_with() does not call it. Here the forged data was not used, so the outputs and signatures were still correct.
embit.S3b: embit trusted the false witness UTXO, left the input out of the BIP 352 input set and computed a silent-payment output the recipient can never find. In this case its signatures are also invalid against the real UTXOs, so the transaction could not be broadcast. The BIP 375 reference validator accepts the result too, which suggests a new invalid test vector.
embit.CTRL-CHANGE: Signed correctly. embit's silent-payments code does not decide which outputs are the user's change, so change handling can only be judged on the devices built on it.
embit.S1: Signed with correct outputs. Whether the host's output would be shown as change cannot be seen at library level: embit leaves change detection to the device.
embit.S2: Signed with correct outputs. Whether the lock-and-ransom output would be shown as change cannot be seen at library level: embit leaves change detection to the device.
embit.S9c1: embit stops with its multi-party message and reports input 1 as belonging to another signer. This case has one signer and a NUMS taproot input that needs no share, so it is recorded as a skip, not a pass.
embit.S9d: embit counts its own input despite the host's NUMS claim: the outputs and signatures are correct. The BIP 375 reference validator is not applied to this case, because the returned PSBT still carries the host's NUMS marking and the validator would drop that input.
embit.S9c1-TR: embit stops with its multi-party message, as for S9c1. A NUMS input needs no share, but it is still another party's input, so this is recorded as a skip.

krux.S7: Krux recognises an output labeled 0xFFFFFFFF as its own and derives the labeled key correctly. It lists it as a self-transfer, which is right: only label 0 is change.
krux.CTRL-MIXED: Skipped: Krux accepts one script type per transaction, so it refuses P2WPKH and P2TR inputs together. A missing feature, not a verdict.
krux.P5: Skipped for the same reason as CTRL-MIXED: this case mixes a silent-payment (P2TR) input with an ordinary P2WPKH input.
krux.CTRL-MULTI: Skipped: Krux does not sign for inputs belonging to another party, so the multi-party cases (S5a, S5b, S8) cannot be run.
krux.CTRL-SEND: Krux exports a trimmed PSBT without the input derivations. The adapter combines it with the PSBT that was sent, as a coordinator would, before judging. Judged on its own the trimmed PSBT fails the BIP 375 reference validator because the input public keys are gone.
krux.S9c2: Krux refuses, which is the required outcome, but with 'missing non_witness_utxo on a legacy input': it read the input as a legacy script, not as segwit v2. The pass shows it does not sign this transaction; it does not show Krux checks for segwit v2 specifically.
krux.S9c1: Skipped: the NUMS taproot input belongs to another party, which Krux does not sign for (and it also refuses to mix P2WPKH with taproot inputs).
krux.S9d: Skipped for the same reason as S9c1: the case needs a P2WPKH and a taproot input in one transaction.
krux.D1: Krux shows the full tsp1 address, in groups, on the spend screen.
krux.D3: Krux shows the full labeled tsp1 address.
krux.CTRL-CHANGE: Krux signs and shows the user's own label-0 change as a payment ("Spend") with its address to verify, not as change. That is deliberate: its code says only a wallet loaded as a Silent Payments wallet owns SP outputs, so for a plain BIP 84 wallet an output to the seed's own sp1 address stays a payment to check. BIP 375 makes change detection optional, so this is safe and recorded as a pass with a note. S1 and S2 are the dangerous direction, a host-keyed output shown as change, and Krux passes them.
krux.S3b: Krux refuses with 'mixed inputs in the tx', which is its one-script-type rule. The refusal is the required outcome; the reason is not specific to the forged witness UTXO.
krux.S9c1-TR: Skipped: the NUMS taproot input is another party's, and Krux stops with 'input(s) 1 belong to another signer'. An input that needs no share still counts as another signer's input.
krux.CTRL-TR: Krux signs two taproot inputs and derives the right outputs: the one-script-type version of CTRL-MIXED.
krux.S9d-TR: Krux signs and derives outputs that include its own input even though the host marked it as NUMS. The BIP 375 reference validator is not applied to this case, because the returned PSBT keeps the host's NUMS marking.
krux.P5-TR: An SP-received input and an ordinary taproot input together: Krux signs and the outputs are right.
krux.S9c3: Krux refuses, which is the required outcome, but with 'Unable to get policy': it could not classify the input, not because it recognised segwit v2. The pass does not show an explicit segwit v2 check.

rust-psbt.CTRL-SEND: rust-psbt checks and signs; it does not compute silent-payment data. For this target the adapter plays the caller: it adds the signer's own ECDH shares and DLEQ proofs and hands the crate the output scripts derived with SilentWitness's own BIP 352 code. A pass here means the crate's Signer rules accept a correct PSBT, not that the crate derives anything itself.
rust-psbt.S4: Refused with ScriptMismatch, but only because the adapter supplied the correctly derived script and the crate compared it with the host's. rust-psbt does not derive scripts, so a caller that skips that step would sign the host's script. The result tests the crate together with the adapter's caller step.
rust-psbt.S6b: Same as S4: the crate refuses the swapped scripts only because the correctly derived ones were supplied for comparison.
rust-psbt.S3b: Refused on the crate's own funding-UTXO rule (witness and non-witness UTXO disagree). The adapter's caller step runs first, so the error is reported by the commit step, not by the signing session.
rust-psbt.S9d: The host marked one of the signer's own taproot inputs as NUMS and the crate refuses with TaprootInternalKeyMismatch (the claimed internal key does not produce the prevout). The case allows a refusal.
rust-psbt.S6a: Skipped: a refusal here would only show that the output scripts were never derived. The crate has no BIP 352 code, and this case has too many outputs to derive them in the suite.
rust-psbt.CTRL-KMAX: Skipped for the same reason as S6a.
rust-psbt.CTRL-MULTI: Skipped: the adapter holds one signer's keys and cannot produce another party's ECDH shares. The multi-party cases (S5a, S5b, S8, S9c1, S9c1-TR) are skipped for the same reason.
rust-psbt.CTRL-SPEND: Skipped: rust-psbt has no BIP 376 support, so it cannot spend silent-payment inputs. The spending cases (P1-P5, P5-TR) are skipped for the same reason.
rust-psbt.CTRL-CHANGE: Signed correctly. The crate has no concept of change detection, so change handling cannot be judged here.
rust-psbt.BIP375-V02: Skipped: this v1.1.1 vector uses a placeholder prevout script that no key hashes to. rust-psbt checks the input key against the prevout and refuses, correctly. The crate's own regenerated v1.2.0 vectors fix the prevouts; the other skipped valid vectors are the same.
rust-psbt.D1: Skipped: the crate has no screen. Display cases need a device.
rust-psbt.EXT375-I17: Skipped: the crate signed, but this case is about a DLEQ proof, which rust-psbt leaves to its caller by design (its own test for this vector is ignored). The BIP 375 reference code refuses the returned PSBT, so the check works at the caller level. The same applies to I20, I47 and I48 (derived scripts).
rust-psbt.EXT375-I10: Skipped: refused only because no output script was ever derived; the crate does not derive them. The same applies to I18.
rust-psbt.EXT375-V03: Skipped: the vector gives a P2WPKH input with only a witness UTXO. rust-psbt's strict signer refuses to sign it without the previous transaction (BIP 174). The crate's own tests sign this vector with the checks switched off.

bitbox02.BB-CTRL-SEND: Signed correctly. The device generated the silent-payment output itself and it matches the independent BIP 352 derivation; every signature verifies.
bitbox02.BB-CTRL-TR: Signed correctly with two taproot inputs; the generated output matches the independent derivation.
bitbox02.BB-CTRL-MIXED: Signed correctly with a P2WPKH and a taproot input together; the generated output matches the independent derivation.
bitbox02.BB-S2: Refused with 'invalid input'. The host marks a receive-branch output as the user's own and adds its own sp1 address. The firmware source rejects any output that is the device's own and carries a silent-payment address ('Receiving on silent payments is not supported yet'); the valid control (BB-CTRL-SEND) signs. Older firmware (before 9.26.3) let a receive-branch keypath through.
bitbox02.BB-S3a: Refused with 'invalid input' when input 0's previous transaction does not hash to its txid. The valid control signs. The firmware hashes each streamed previous transaction and compares it with the input's prevout hash, which matches this refusal; it skips that check when every input is taproot, so a taproot-only version of this case is a different question.
bitbox02.BB-S9a: Counted as correct because the device signed with SIGHASH_ALL (every signature ends in 0x01) although the PSBT asked for SIGHASH_NONE. The firmware reads no sighash from the host and signs SIGHASH_ALL only (SIGHASH_DEFAULT for taproot). A refusal would also be correct.
bitbox02.BB-S9b: Same as S9a for SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY: the device signed with SIGHASH_ALL, so the host's value had no effect on what was signed.
bitbox02.BB-D1: The device shows the full sp1 address, in groups of four characters, on its payment confirmation screen, next to the amount, then a fee screen.
bitbox02.BB-D3: The device shows the full labeled sp1 address. It differs from the unlabeled address in the spend-key part, so the label is visible to the user.

kern.CTRL-KMAX: Signed correctly with 2,323 silent-payment outputs to one scan key; the derived scripts and signatures verify.
kern.S1: Refused: output 1 claims our key origin but its spend key is not ours, so Kern's ownership gate stops it ('carries our fingerprint but cannot be verified'). Refusing is safe; signing it as an external payment is the other correct result, so the case allows both.
kern.S2: Refused by the same ownership gate as S1: output 1 claims our key origin with a scan key we do not hold. A refusal is allowed.
kern.S3a: Refused at the gate with 'invalid input amount': the forged previous transaction does not hash to the input's txid.
kern.S3b: Refused at the gate with 'invalid input amount': the witness UTXO contradicts the previous transaction.
kern.S4: Refused during the BIP 375 share round: 'Output script differs from its silent payment'.
kern.S6a: Refused with 'Malformed silent payment field' at K_max + 1 outputs to one scan key; the control with exactly K_max signs.
kern.S6b: Refused: 'Output script differs from its silent payment' when the pre-filled scripts have k swapped.
kern.S9a: Refused when the PSBT is read: Kern rejects a sighash other than SIGHASH_ALL beside silent-payment outputs.
kern.S9b: Refused when the PSBT is read, as S9a, for SIGHASH_ALL|ANYONECANPAY.
kern.S9c2: Refused, but by the partial-signing gate ('inputs of other signers'), not by the BIP 375 segwit v2 rule: the v2 input is another party's, so this case cannot tell the two apart.
kern.S9c3: Refused by the partial-signing gate for the same reason as S9c2.
kern.S9d: Refused with 'an input the policy cleared could not be signed' when the host marks the device's own taproot input as NUMS. A refusal is allowed.
kern.S9d-TR: Same as S9d on a taproot-only transaction.
kern.P1: Refused by the partial-signing gate: with a tweak that does not match, Kern does not recognise the input as its own and treats it as another signer's. It signs nothing, but not through a tweak check of its own.
kern.P2: Refused by the partial-signing gate for the same reason as P1.
